text.p: AOOT Chernogorneft said on Thursday its pre-tax profit in the first three quarters of 1996 fell to $35.6 million from $40.4 million a year earlier, while net sales rose to $247.9 million from $235.0 million.
The unaudited figures from the oil firm are to Russian accounting standards using the old cash-based accounting system.

According to the new Russian accruals-based accounting standards, for which comparisons are not available, pre-tax profit in the first three quarters of this year was $53.7 million on net sales of $362.4 million.
Chernogorneft has also published 1994 and 1995 full-year figures audited by Ernst & Young to U.S. GAAP.
NOTES - The following dollar/rouble exchange rates are used.

Balance sheet items as of October 1. Total output includes output from three joint ventures and production-sharing agreements with local service companies. Reserves are annual audit by Miller and Lents less period's output. Oil sales represent only oil actually paid for, not total deliveries.

Full name AOOT Chernogorneft. As of October 1, 1996, NK Sidanko owned 37.7 percent and Uneximbank (Oneksimbank in Russian) and affiliates Bank MFK (IFCI) and Moscow Partners 14.7 percent. Another 17.1 percent was held in American Depositary Receipts through Bank of New York, and 6.3 percent in Russian Depositary Receipts through ING Barings. Other foreign entities owned 13.0 percent, individual shareholders 7.5 percent, other Russian entities 2.0 percent, Treasury stock 1.7 percent.

The Uneximbank group has control over Chernogorneft, as Bank MFK backed by Uneximbank won control of 51 percent of Sidanko under the government's shares-for-loans programme. In September InterRos Oil acquired 34 percent of Sidanko and must transfer 13 percent of Chernogorneft to Sidanko. The Interros group includes Uneximbank and MFK.

These figures are not prepared to international accounting standards but to Russian accounting standards, which differ significantly from those normally used in the West and which are designed to meet the requirements of the tax authorities.
Definitions of profit and assets differ significantly from those in the West, and converting Russian accounts to international standards can turn a profit into a loss.
Figures are not adjusted for inflation. Consumer prices in September 1996 were 16.5 percent higher than in December 1995. In September 1995 they were 104.7 percent higher than in December 1994.
